title: Argenx to buy peptide platform in potentially billion-dollar deal
content: An article from Dive Brief Argenx to buy peptide platform in potentially billion-dollar deal For $550 million up front, Argenx will take control of Unnatural Products’ “macrocyclic peptide” technology and direct it to develop oral, durable medicines for serious immune-mediated diseases. Published Nov. 9, 2026 Jacob Bell Lead Reporter Share Copy link Email LinkedIn X/Twitter Facebook Print License Add us on Google Argenx agreed to acquire Unnatural Products, a maker of "macrocyclic peptides," on Nov. 9, 2026. deliormanli via Getty Images Dive Brief: Argenx, a Netherlands-based biotechnology company focused on antibody drugs, on Monday said it has agreed to acquire a protein specialist in a potentially billion-dollar-plus deal. Unnatural Products has a platform that pairs machine learning, screening and other techniques to engineer “macrocyclic peptides.” These peptides are larger and more complex than typical small molecules, which allows them to more effectively bind to tricky proteins and address some challenging diseases. Yet, they’re still tiny enough that they can be swallowed. Argenx plans to use the platform to develop oral, durable medicines for serious immune-mediated diseases. The acquisition carries a $550 million upfront cash payment. Unnatural Products could receive up to $595 million more if specific milestones are hit. In 2020, for example, Rhythm Pharmaceuticals’ Imcivree was cleared as a treatment for certain genetic forms of obesity. The following year, Aurinia Pharmaceuticals’ Lupkynis became the first-ever oral medicine for adults with active lupus nephritis. In 2023, the FDA greenlit a UCB medicine called Zilbrysq for “generalized myasthenia gravis,” a rare autoimmune condition that’s become somewhat of a battleground for several developers. Argenx’s own flagship product, Vyvgart, targets this disease and brought in $4.5 billion in net product sales from January through the end of September. Thomas Smith, a Leerink Partners analyst who covers Argenx, wrote in a note to clients that the new acquisition “represents potential for longer-term strategic value.” He explained there’s a desire — both in big pharma and in the broader immunology and inflammation research space — to make oral, long-acting therapeutics that are able to be more effective and convenient than conventional biologics. The Unnatural Products deal, which comes on the heels of Argenx’s potentially $2.2 billion purchase of Forte Biosciences, also “signals further focus on pipeline growth and diversification,” Smith wrote. title: Bayer wins FDA nod for a new kind of blood thinner
content: An article from Bayer wins FDA nod for a new kind of blood thinner Sunharbo’s U.S. approval is the first for a “Factor XIa” inhibitor, an anticipated class of medicines seen as a possible step forward in stroke prevention. Published Nov. 9, 2026 Jacob Bell Lead Reporter Share Copy link Email LinkedIn X/Twitter Facebook Print License Add us on Google The FDA approved Bayer's blood thinning drug Sunharbo on Nov. 9, 2026. Permission granted by Bayer The Food and Drug Administration on Monday approved a new kind of blood thinner meant to lower the risk of stroke in certain adults, marking a major milestone for cardiovascular research as well as the medicine’s developer, Bayer. The pill, which will be sold under the brand name Sunharbo, doesn’t work like established stroke prevention drugs. It inhibits a blood-clotting protein called Factor XIa. While this protein plays a minor role in sealing up blood vessels after an injury, it also amplifies a coagulation “cascade” that helps clots grow and makes them harder to break down, increasing the risk of strokes or heart attacks. if (window.dfp_visibility === 'mobile' ) { googletag.cmd.push(function() { googletag.defineSlot( '/3618/biopharmadive/biopharmadivehybrid1', [[300, 250], 'fluid'], 'dfp-hybrid1-mobile' ).addService(googletag.pubads()); The large study that led to its approval enrolled more than 12,000 adults who previously had either a “warning stroke” or a stroke caused by a blood clot that originated outside of the heart. About half of the participants got a placebo, the other half once-daily Sunharbo, and all received antiplatelet therapy. Results showed Bayer’s drug reduced the risk of the most common, “ischemic” form of stroke by 26% compared to the control arm. The study also found that the number of major bleeding cases was similar across the two groups. The most frequently reported adverse reaction among Sunharbo-treated patients was diarrhea. The FDA has now cleared Sunharbo, which is known scientifically as asundexian, for secondary stroke prevention in this patient population, to be used alongside antiplatelet therapy. Health authorities estimate more than 795,000 people in the U.S. have a stroke each year, with about a quarter having experienced one previously. “When you spend time with physicians in this space, they will tell you that they see asundexian [as] practice-changing,” said Sebastian Guth, chief operating officer of Bayer Pharmaceuticals and president of Bayer U.S. It has “very significant utility for the patients they serve.” The head of Bayer’s pharmaceuticals division, Stefan Oelrich, said during an earnings call in August that his team expects doctors, especially in the acute treatment setting, to “broadly welcome” Sunharbo. And if the launch has one “limiting factor,” it will be access. if (window.dfp_visibility === 'mobile' ) { googletag.cmd.push(function() { googletag.defineSlot( '/3618/biopharmadive/biopharmadivehybrid2', [[300, 250], 'fluid'], 'dfp-hybrid2-mobile' ).addService(googletag.pubads()); }); } waitToLoadAds.push(function() { googletag.cmd.push(function() { if (window.dfp_visibility === 'mobile' ) { window.onDvtagReady?.(() => googletag.display('dfp-hybrid2-mobile')); googletag.pubads().addEventListener('slotRenderEnded', function (event) { var adUnitPath = '/3618/biopharmadive/biopharmadivehybrid2'; var onProformative = false; if (onProformative && event.slot.getAdUnitPath() === adUnitPath && !event.isEmpty ) { var adUnitPathWithVisibility = adUnitPath + '-mobile'; var selector = '.pf-comments__ad-wrapper #dfp-hybrid2-mobile'; if (!$(selector).closest('.pf-comments__ad-wrapper').hasClass('borders')) { $(selector).closest('.pf-comments__ad-wrapper').addClass('borders') } } }); } }); }); According to Guth, stroke neurologists will be a “very important part” of the drug’s early rollout, as they are often the first in line to treat these patients. Over time, primary care physicians will be a greater focus. While the company hasn’t disclosed what or how many treatment centers it plans to initially target, Guth said it has set up a “very robust” patient support program. Payers, he added, already recognize the merits of a drug like Sunharbo. Heart disease and stroke killed more than 850,000 people in the U.S. in 2024, according to the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention. The agency anticipates that costs from cardiovascular diseases are on track to reach roughly $2 trillion by 2050. “It requires innovation to first and foremost benefit patients, but also to bend the curve [on] the economic burden of stroke and heart disease,” Guth said. “That's what we're into. That's what we're focused on, and that does resonate with payers.” A 30-day supply of Sunharbo will have a list price of $748.50, according to a Bayer spokesperson. Bayer has experience in this arena, having for years sold the blockbuster blood thinner Xarelto outside the U.S. Xarelto inhibits a different clotting protein, “Factor Xa,” and has experienced a sales decline due to generic competition. Bayer recorded 738 million euros, or around $860 million, from Xarelto over the first six months of 2026 — an almost 43% drop from the same period a year prior. If analyst forecasts are any indication, the new class of drugs that includes Sunharbo could become multibillion-dollar products. Bristol Myers Squibb and Johnson & Johnson are jointly developing one, milvexian, that has suffered multiple setbacks in clinical testing. Yet Leerink Partners analysts earlier this month still modeled $2.5 billion in risk-adjusted sales of milvexian in 2032, while acknowledging that the drug could disappoint in two large, ongoing trials evaluating it against stroke and atrial fibrillation. (Sunharbo, too, stumbled in a key atrial fibrillation experiment.) Elsewhere, rival developers are taking aim at Factor XIa in different ways. Novartis has continued work on an injectable antibody therapy acquired through its $925 million purchase of Anthos Therapeutics in 2025. City Therapeutics, which just went public, also has an RNA-based medicine that's in early-stage testing. The Food and Drug Administration on Monday approved Bayer’s drug to reduce recurrence of stroke, making available the first in a novel class of medications that hold the promise of preventing blood clots more safely. Many blood thinners aren’t used in this setting due to the increased risk of bleeding. But Bayer’s drug, which will be sold under the brand name Sunharbo, inhibits a protein called XIa, utilizing a mechanism that’s thought to stop the formation of bad clots without increasing the risk of bleeding.Advertisement Related Story Lowering blood pressure after stroke or with diabetes poses challenges, in research and practice In a Phase 3 trial that enrolled people who had already had a stroke and were taking common stroke treatments, 8.4% of participants who took placebo experienced a secondary stroke, while 6.2% of patients who took Sunharbo experienced one, translating into a 26% risk reduction. The Food and Drug Administration on Monday warned that GLP-1 drugs carry a potential risk for a rare but serious eye condition and required pharma companies to inform patients and doctors of the risk. The condition, called non-arteritic anterior ischemic optic neuropathy, or NAION, is sometimes referred to as an “eye stroke” and is caused by insufficient blood flow to the optic nerve. It typically causes sudden vision loss and, in severe cases, can lead to blindness. There are currently no proven treatments for the condition.Advertisement Related Story STAT Plus: Study links Ozempic to higher risk of eye condition that can cause vision loss GLP-1 drugs such as Novo Nordisk’s Ozempic and Wegovy and Eli Lilly’s Mounjaro and Zepbound have exploded in popularity for their potent weight loss effects, but as with any drugs that are given to large populations, side effects can show up in real-world use that weren’t observed in clinical trials. content: 首页 资讯 摩熵原创 时讯 AASLD 2026公布Bepirovirsen最新临床数据，实现乙肝功能性治愈后持续应答达21个月， 国内上市在即 AASLD 2026公布Bepirovirsen最新临床数据，实现乙肝功能性治愈后持续应答达21个月， 国内上市在即 张鹏 · 新药研发分析师 张 张鹏 新药研发分析师 审核：王正晴 · 药学博士 关注全球创新药研发管线、临床试验进展与注册审批动态；重点分析热门靶点、临床价值与管线竞争格局。累计发布研发分析 102+ 篇。 15小时前 798 乙肝 乙肝功能性治愈 乙肝新药最新动态 Bepirovirsen AASLD 乙肝新药最新动态来了！我国约有7500万慢性乙肝病毒感染者，全球首款乙肝功能性治愈创新药Bepirovirsen有望即将在中国获批上市。在2026年美国肝病研究学会（AASLD）年会上，全球首款乙肝功能性治愈创新药Bepirovirsen全球大三期B-Well研究公布96周持久性随访数据：在实现功能性治愈的患者中，91%在停药一年后仍维持治愈状态。也即，绝大多数患者实现功能性治愈后未复发。图源：中国生物制药企业官微一、91%治愈者“守得住”，免疫系统真正接管此次重磅数据，由南方医科大学南方医院侯金林教授、香港大学袁孟峰教授在AASLD现场向全球学者报告。该临床数据显示，在第72周实现功能性治愈的受试者中，继续随访至第96周时，91%仍维持功能性治愈；病毒学抑制率同样高达96%。这一结果在乙肝表面抗原不同基线人群中高度一致。什么是“功能性治愈”？简单说，就是患者完成有限疗程治疗后，乙肝表面抗原和病毒DNA持续检测不到，经医生评估可以停药，停药后病毒不再反弹。简单来说，这次数据的重要性，在于回答了“患者治愈之后能维持多久”这一核心问题。过去，乙肝患者只能依靠长期服药抑制病毒，一旦停药往往反弹。现在，经过有限疗程治疗后，绝大多数患者的免疫系统能够真正“接管”病毒控制，停药后长期不复发。值得关注的是，这不是小规模研究的结果。B-Well两项研究，是覆盖29个国家、纳入1838名患者的全球多中心、随机双盲对照三期临床，是目前全球乙肝领域规模最大的治愈研究之一。同期另一项研究结果B-Sure研究也验证，功能性治愈一旦实现即具有可持续性。在 B-Well 研究中实现功能性治愈并维持到96周的受试者，大部分(95%)受试者至少可以维持15个月，即停止全部乙肝治疗后至少维持21个月的持续应答。图源：摩熵医药-全球药物研发数据库安全性方面，B-well研究显示在73-96周停药随访期内，未发现与Bepirovirsen相关的迟发安全风险，药物相关不良反应发生率仅为2%，且多为轻度、单发事件。二、从“终身服药”到“有限疗程”，治疗范式正在改变按照疾病发展路径，慢性乙肝若未规范治疗，可能沿“肝炎-肝硬化-肝癌”的路径进展，甚至有直接进展为肝癌的风险。研究显示，实现功能性治愈的患者，5年肝癌发生率可降至1%以内，与正常人基本一致。据摩熵医药数据库显示，目前，Bepirovirsen在2026年8月24日，日本获批上市，10月20日美国获批上市，成为全球首个且唯一获得多国监管认定的乙肝功能性治愈新药，为全球乙肝患者迈向“有限疗程治愈”提供了全新选择。图源：摩熵医药-全球药物研发数据库世界卫生组织提出“2030年消除病毒性肝炎作为公共卫生危害”目标。业内专家表示，随着功能性治愈药物逐步可及，乙肝“可治愈、守得住”的时代正在到来。更多乙肝新药进展，可点击→2026年乙肝新药最新进展~持续更新中参考来源：[1] 企业官微/官方披露[2] 摩熵医药（原药融云）数据库扩展阅读：1. 2026乙肝新药最新消息！GSK全球首款功能性治愈药Bepirovirsen获批上市，同日PD-1单抗获优先审评2. 中国生物制药联手GSK加速全球首款乙肝功能性治愈新药Bepirovirsen在华上市，瞄准700亿大市场3. 2026大会常规摘要公开，先声药业自主研发的三特异性抗体SIM0500（SCR-8572）首次披露临床数据。图源：ASH官网I期研究结果显示，在剂量8—12队列中，SIM0500的客观缓解率（ORR）达到81.3%，9例可评估患者全部达到微小残留病灶（MRD）阴性。一、靶向三大靶点，ORR达到81.3%SIM0500是一款靶向CD3、BCMA和GPRC5D的三特异性抗体，其中BCMA为单价结合域，GPRC5D为双价结合域。该药通过降低CD3结合亲和力、增强BCMA和GPRC5D结合亲和力，旨在兼顾治疗效果与安全性。图源：摩熵医药-全球药物研发数据库截至2026年6月22日，其I期临床研究共纳入38例既往接受过至少三线治疗的复发或难治性多发性骨髓瘤（RRMM）患者，评估了12个剂量水平，中位随访时间为7.53个月。疗效方面，在剂量8—12队列中，16例患者可评估疗效，ORR达到81.3%，其中75%的患者获得非常好的部分缓解（VGPR），37.5%达到完全缓解（CR）。在剂量10—12队列中，7例患者的ORR达到85.7%，其中71.4%获得VGPR，28.6%达到CR。此外，3例既往接受过BCMA或GPRC5D靶向药物治疗的患者中，有2例获得VGPR。MRD检测结果同样值得关注：9例可评估患者全部达到MRD阴性，中位缓解时间为4.7周。同时，剂量8—12队列患者在第二个治疗周期第1天（C2D1）的游离血清BCMA水平较基线下降93.2%。摩熵医药全球药物研发数据库显示，SIM0500此前已获得跨国药企艾伯维的关注。2025年1月，先声再明与艾伯维就SIM0500达成海外许可选择权协议。图源：摩熵医药-全球药物研发数据库根据协议，先声方面将获得首付款，以及最高10.55亿美元的选择性权益付款和里程碑付款，此外还可获得该产品在大中华区以外地区净销售额的分级特许权使用费。二、安全性可控，未出现剂量限制性毒性安全性方面，在38例患者中，未观察到剂量限制性毒性（DLT），治疗期间不良事件（TEAE）发生率为63.2%，且没有患者因毒性终止治疗。细胞因子释放综合征（CRS）发生率为44.7%，其中36.8%为1级、7.9%为2级，未出现3级及以上事件。CRS具有可预测性，82.4%的事件发生在首次给药后，中位发作时间为17.8小时，中位缓解时间为12.0小时。此外，未报告免疫效应细胞相关神经毒性综合征（ICANS）。其他不良事件方面，感染发生率为39.5%，其中13.2%为3级，未出现4级及5级事件；非皮疹皮肤病发生率为57.9%，其中1级和2级分别占39.5%和18.4%，未出现3级事件。味觉障碍发生率为34.2%，指甲疾病发生率为31.6%，后者均为1级事件。总体来看，SIM0500在此次披露的I期研究中展现出初步抗肿瘤活性，尤其是剂量8—12队列的缓解率及MRD阴性结果值得关注。同时，研究尚处于早期阶段，后续仍需更大样本量和更长随访时间进一步验证其疗效与安全性。参考来源：[1] title: 翰宇药业HY3003获FDA临床许可！国产GLP-1/GIP/GCGR三重激动剂出海提速，减重效果优于替尔泊肽
content: 首页 资讯 摩熵原创 时讯 翰宇药业HY3003获FDA临床许可！国产GLP-1/GIP/GCGR三重激动剂出海提速，减重效果优于替尔泊肽 翰宇药业HY3003获FDA临床许可！国产GLP-1/GIP/GCGR三重激动剂出海提速，减重效果优于替尔泊肽 张鹏 · 新药研发分析师 张 张鹏 新药研发分析师 审核：王正晴 · 药学博士 关注全球创新药研发管线、临床试验进展与注册审批动态；重点分析热门靶点、临床价值与管线竞争格局。累计发布研发分析 102+ 篇。 昨天 15:13 1920 GCGR GIPR GLP-1R 替尔泊肽 深圳翰宇药业股份有限公司 全球减重药市场的竞争，正从单靶点、双靶点向多靶点延伸。继替尔泊肽之后，国产三靶点减重药也迎来新进展。11月5日，翰宇药业（300199.SZ）发布公告，公司近日收到美国食品药品监督管理局（FDA）关于HY3003注射液（IND编号：184763）的临床试验许可通知。这款同时靶向GLP-1R、GIPR和GCGR的三重受体激动剂，正式获得进入美国临床试验的资格。图源：翰宇药业企业公告值得关注的是，HY3003在临床前研究中展现出一定的减重潜力，而翰宇药业前三季度归母净利润同比增长511.96%，多肽原料药业务持续放量。一、三靶点机制加持，临床前减重效果优于替尔泊肽HY3003是翰宇药业布局的一款新型GLP-1R/GIPR/GCGR三重受体激动剂，拟通过同时激活三种受体，实现对体重、血糖及代谢指标的综合调节。在剂型布局上，公司采用多剂型并行开发策略，涵盖每周注射一次的HY3003注射液、每月注射一次的缓释注射液，以及每日一次的口服片剂。本次获得FDA临床试验许可的是HY3003注射液，给药方式为每周皮下注射一次。图源：摩熵医药-全球药物研发数据库从临床前研究来看，HY3003已展现出一定的药效学潜力。根据公司披露的研究结果，在同等摩尔剂量下，HY3003注射液在饮食诱导肥胖（DIO）小鼠模型中的减重效果优于已上市的双靶点激动剂替尔泊肽及在研三靶点激动剂瑞他曲肽。同时，该药在降糖、减脂及改善肝脏脂肪变性等方面也表现出良好的药效学特征。需要强调的是，上述结果来自临床前动物实验，尚不能代表其在人体中的实际减重效果，后续仍需通过临床研究验证。研发进度方面，HY3003于2026年10月5日获得FDA IND受理，约30天后即取得临床试验许可。公司披露，本次IND审评全程未收到FDA信息请求（Information Request，IR），FDA已完成安全性审查，同意公司按照提交的临床试验方案开展首次临床试验。国内方面，摩熵医药数据库显示，HY3003相关临床试验申请目前处于审评阶段。图源：摩熵医药-全球药物研发数据库根据公告披露，HY3003-001是一项在健康成人参与者中开展的首次人体研究，采用单次递增剂量、单中心、随机、双盲、安慰剂对照设计，主要评估药物的安全性、耐受性、药代动力学、药效学及免疫原性。这意味着，HY3003目前仍处于首次人体研究阶段，现阶段重点是评估药物在健康成人中的安全性及相关药代、药效特征，尚未进入肥胖患者中的减重疗效验证阶段。二、净利润增长超5倍，翰宇药业多肽业务持续放量从公司整体业务来看，翰宇药业长期深耕多肽药物领域，业务覆盖多肽制剂、原料药、小核酸及医药研发生产服务。在GLP-1药物领域，公司已布局利拉鲁肽、司美格鲁肽、替尔泊肽等产品。其中，利拉鲁肽注射液已获美国FDA批准，替尔泊肽仿制药的美国ANDA申请已获受理。此次HY3003取得FDA临床试验许可，则进一步拓展了公司在原创新药领域的布局。从公司此前披露的创新药管线图来看，除HY3003外，翰宇药业还布局了HY3000鼻喷雾剂和HY3001多肽疫苗。其中，HY3000用于预防和治疗新型冠状病毒感染，HY3001用于预防新型冠状病毒感染；HY3003则面向减重和2型糖尿病等代谢疾病领域。图源：翰宇药业企业官网业绩方面，翰宇药业2026年三季报显示，前三季度公司实现营业收入12.42亿元，同比增长81.87%；归母净利润4.37亿元，同比增长511.96%；扣非归母净利润4.28亿元，同比增长741.83%。其中，第三季度单季实现营业收入5.54亿元，同比增长314.48%；归母净利润约2亿元，同比增长369.76%。前三季度经营活动产生的现金流量净额为3.78亿元，同比增长39.77%；研发费用为1.61亿元，同比增长117.11%。图源：翰宇药业第三季度报告公司业绩增长主要受多肽原料药业务持续放量带动。随着相关业务规模扩大，公司也在推进创新药研发和国际化布局。 从全球研发趋势来看，减重药物竞争正逐步向多靶点方向延伸。礼来在研的瑞他曲肽同样作用于GLP-1R、GIPR和GCGR，与HY3003具有相同的三靶点作用机制。未来，相关产品的竞争不仅取决于靶点数量，还将涉及减重效果、代谢获益、安全性及给药便利性等多个维度。对于HY3003而言，目前披露的积极信号主要来自临床前研究，后续还需通过I期、II期、III期临床试验，进一步验证其安全性、耐受性和临床疗效。至于月制剂和口服剂型，也有待后续研发进展及临床数据支持。总体来看，HY3003获得FDA临床试验许可，是翰宇药业创新多肽药物国际化推进的重要一步，也为其代谢疾病领域产品管线增加了新的研发项目。不过，从临床前研究走向真正的临床价值，仍有较长的验证过程，最终能否获批上市尚存在不确定性。参考来源：[1] Published Nov. 10, 2026 Jonathan Gardner Senior Reporter Share Copy link Email LinkedIn X/Twitter Facebook Print License Add us on Google Beam Therapeutics is preparing what could be the first FDA submission for a "base editing" treatment. Getty Images Dive Brief: Beam Therapeutics said Tuesday that a precision gene editing treatment it’s been working on succeeded in a pivotal trial, helping free people with sickle cell disease from the severe bouts of pain associated with their condition. The results for ristoglogene autogetemcel, or “risto-cel,” represent the first positive late-stage readout for a drugmaking approach known as “base editing.” Beam says it plans to submit an approval application to the Food and Drug Administration by as soon as the end of the year. Sickle cell disease, a genetic disorder largely affecting people with African ancestry, is already the target of two marketed genetic therapies called Casgevy and Lyfgenia, both of which initially saw slow uptake. Those treatments, however, are built on different underlying technologies. if (!$(selector).closest('.pf-comments__ad-wrapper').hasClass('borders')) { $(selector).closest('.pf-comments__ad-wrapper').addClass('borders') } } }); } }); }); Dive Insight: Base editing is a newer form of gene editing that can precisely change individual nucleotides, or “letters,” in a DNA sequence. The technology offers a pinpoint solution for treating genetic conditions and, in contrast to older CRISPR approaches, doesn’t cut through DNA. Both risto-cel and Casgevy — the latter of which is made with CRISPR technology — are made by extracting and re-engineering patients’ own cells to switch on production of a special oxygen-carrying protein known as “fetal hemoglobin.” Those new cells are then transplanted back into the patient, where they head to the bone marrow and start producing normal blood cells. These biological effects are meant to stop the formation of sickle-shaped blood cells and the painful “vaso-occlusive crises,” or VOCs, they cause. The data Beam released Tuesday came from a group of 31 patients who’d completed treatment and 12 months of follow-up as of Oct. 20. Without releasing specific details, Beam said risto-cel achieved its primary goal of “freedom from severe VOCs.” The treatment hit secondary objectives, such as a reduction in hospital stays associated with VOCs, as well. The data represent a “defining milestone for risto-cel and for Beam’s base editing technology more broadly,” CEO John Evans said in a statement. Should risto-cel gain approval, Beam will compete in a treatment landscape that includes less-invasive drugs like hydroxyurea and l-glutamine, blood transfusions and stem cell transplants. Beam would also be third to market with a genetic therapy for sickle cell, meaning it’ll have to battle with already established therapies in Lyfgenia and Casgevy. The developers of those other medicines, Genetix Biotherapeutics (formerly known as Bluebird Bio) and a partnership between Vertex Pharmaceuticals and CRISPR Therapeutics, struggled early on to sell their therapies. Genetix, for instance, sold itself after having a difficult time marketing Lyfgenia and other gene therapies. And only five people got Casgevy in the second half of 2024. Vertex has since reported an upswing in Casgevy sales, though. The number of patients receiving treatment rose to 64 in 2025, leading to $116 million in total revenue. Vertex then recorded $219 million in Casgevy sales through the first nine months of 2026. Speaking to analysts with RBC Capital Markets in September, Beam’s management team contended that uptake for these kinds of treatments has been limited by “supply constraint[s],” rather than slow demand or reimbursement issues, according to a client note. Risto-cel is likely to be attractive to providers and patients because it has a shorter manufacturing process and requires fewer cycles of treatment to mobilize the gene-edited cells to work, the RBC analysts wrote at the time. content: STAT PlusBiotech Coming readout of Kymera eczema trial is a high-stakes moment in a bid to rival Dupixent Biotech aspires to turn pill into a therapy for multiple immunology and inflammatory disorders Manage alerts for this article Save this story for later Share this article Adobe By Jonathan WosenNov. 2, 2026 West Coast Biotech & Life Sciences Reporter Jonathan Wosen[email protected]Jonathan Wosen is STAT’s West Coast biotech & life sciences reporter. You can reach Jonathan on Signal at jwosen.27. Over the past decade, Sanofi and Regeneron’s Dupixent has become the top-selling drug in immunology, bringing in tens of billions in revenue while transforming outcomes for the 1.4 million patients currently on the therapy for conditions including eczema, asthma, and chronic obstructive pulmonary disease. But investors and doctors are intensely following an experimental therapy positioned to rival the pharma blockbuster, with results from a key study fast approaching. Massachusetts biotech Kymera Therapeutics plans to announce data from a mid-stage clinical trial of its lead asset, KT-621, in eczema before the end of the year. Market analysts for the investment bank Jefferies, using common shorthand for immunology and inflammatory disorders, have called the upcoming results “one of the most impactful I&I readouts this year.” Advertisement Success (or failure) could have major consequences for Kymera, its growing list of competitors, and the millions of people who live with eczema in the United States. The results could also bolster or dampen the biotech’s aspirations to treat a broader class of immunological diseases with its drug, including chronic spontaneous urticaria and asthma. Analysts forecast that the drug’s sales could reach nearly $4 billion by 2035, including more than $3 billion in eczema revenue, according to Visible Alpha. content: Advertisement News|Articles|November 10, 2026 AstraZeneca Acquires Omniose, Adding Bioconjugation Platform to Vaccine Pipeline Author(s)Nicholas Jacobus AstraZeneca acquires Omniose, to bolster it's preclinical infectious disease programs. Advertisement AstraZeneca has entered a deal to acquire Omniose, following a three-year exclusive research collaboration between the two organizations that both sides described as productive.Christian Harding, CSO and co-founder of Omniose, frames the acquisition as the culmination of years of partnership. “This milestone reflects the work of exceptional and complementary teams,” Harding says. “AstraZeneca has been a trusted partner for several years, and this acquisition gives our platform the best chance to reach the patients it was built to serve.”¹Under the terms of the agreement, Omniose is set to become a wholly owned subsidiary of AstraZeneca and will join the company’s Infectious Disease Unit.¹ The deal brings Omniose’s proprietary bioconjugation platform and expertise into AstraZeneca, complementing the larger company’s existing capabilities and supporting its preclinical vaccine programs.¹ Financial details of the deal have yet to be disclosed.What problem does bioconjugation solve?Conventional conjugate vaccine manufacturing requires chemical cross-linking of bacterial polysaccharide antigens to immunogenic carrier proteins, a process that is complex and makes the resulting vaccines difficult to produce reproducibly and to characterize, requiring extensive release testing before use.2 The non-specific nature of that cross-linking, and the conditions chemical conjugation requires, can also lead to undesired modifications of epitopes that may affect the quality of the immune response generated against the polysaccharide antigen.2 Bioconjugation offers what is described as an elegantly simple alternative to chemical conjugation, producing and linking the antigen and carrier protein within a single cell.2 (()=>{var l=(n,t)=>{let infections caused by bacterial pathogens including Haemophilus influenzae type B, Streptococcus pneumoniae, Neisseria meningitidis, and Salmonella typhi.2 These vaccines carry an added public health benefit by preventing the infections they target, while also helping to fight antimicrobial resistance by reducing the overall use of antibiotics.2The underlying bioconjugation science has already moved through clinical development in other hands. Omniose co-founder Mario Feldman provided the work leading to the industrialization of bioconjugate vaccine technologies by GSK, following that company’s acquisition of GlycoVaxyn/Limmatech’s bioconjugate platform technology, for vaccine candidates against Shigella, which is now in Phase IIB development, and Klebsiella pneumoniae, now in Phase I development.2Janssen, now known as Johnson & that candidate into Phase III development.2Benjamin Moutier, senior vice president, infectious disease, AstraZeneca, points to the scientific differentiation Omniose’s platform offers. “Omniose’s bioconjugation platform represents a differentiated approach to engineering conjugate vaccines and strengthens our ability to develop novel vaccines against serious bacterial infections,” Moutier says. “Building on the strong scientific collaboration between our teams, we look forward to advancing these programs and realizing the potential of this technology for patients.”What comes next for the combined vaccine programs?With the acquisition complete, Omniose’s bioconjugation platform now sits inside AstraZeneca’s Infectious Disease Unit, where it is positioned to support the unit’s existing preclinical vaccine programs targeting serious bacterial infections.1Timothy Cooke, CEO of Omniose, describes the acquisition as a shared win built around a common mission. “The acquisition by AstraZeneca is a great outcome for both organizations,” Cooke says. “We share a vision for bringing the best science and talent together to address serious bacterial infections, which are title: FDA Approves asundexian for Secondary Stroke Risk Reduction
content: Advertisement News|Articles|November 10, 2026 FDA Approves asundexian for Secondary Stroke Risk Reduction Author(s)Nicholas Jacobus FDA approves Bayer’s asundexian (Sunharbo), the first Factor XIa inhibitor, for secondary stroke prevention. Advertisement FDA has granted marketing authorization for asundexian, 50 mg tablets, to be sold under the brand name Sunharbo, making it the first approved Factor XIa inhibitor worldwide.The product is indicated for use in combination with antiplatelet therapy to reduce the risk of stroke in adults with a recent non-cardioembolic ischemic stroke (National Institutes of Health Stroke Scale ≤15) or high-risk transient ischemic attack (TIA).1 This use is often referred to as secondary stroke prevention, reflecting the goal of reducing the risk of another stroke after an initial event.The approval addresses a period that clinicians consider dangerous for stroke survivors, as the risk of a second potentially devastating event is highest in the days and weeks immediately following an initial stroke, and that elevated risk persists over time.1 Stroke remains a significant global health burden, affecting approximately 12 million people worldwide each year, including 795,000 individuals in the U.S., and is the second leading cause of death and the third leading cause of death and disability combined worldwide.1“This FDA approval represents a bold step forward in post-stroke care.”Christian Rommel, Ph.D., global head of research and development at Bayer’s Pharmaceuticals Division, calls the approval a milestone built on the completed Oceanic-stroke study. “This FDA approval represents a bold step forward in post-stroke care and is based on compelling clinical evidence from our successfully completed Oceanic-stroke study. Asundexian is the first drug approved in a new class of Factor XIa inhibitors worldwide,” Rommel says. “Stroke requires substantial healthcare resource utilization and presents a significant economic and personal burden. At Bayer, our priority is advancing innovations like asundexian to help close gaps in care and reduce the burden of secondary stroke.”What clinical evidence supported the approval?FDA’s approval is based on positive data from the pivotal, global Phase III Oceanic-stroke study, described as the first successfully completed Phase III study of a Factor XIa inhibitor used in combination with antiplatelet therapy.2 The study demonstrated superiority in reducing ischemic stroke compared to antiplatelet therapy alone (dual or single antiplatelet therapy), with a similar rate of major bleeding, as classified by the International Society on Thrombosis and Hemostasis (ISTH), between asundexian and placebo.2 (()=>{var l=(n,t)=>{let i=async()=>{await(await n())()},e=typeof t.value=="object"?t.value:void 0,s={timeout:e==null?void 0:e.timeout};"requestIdleCallback"in window?window.requestIdleCallback(i,s):setTimeout(i,s.timeout||200)};(self.Astro||(self.Astro={})).idle=l;window.dispatchEvent(new Event("astro:idle"));})(); Asundexian 50 mg in combination with antiplatelet therapy significantly reduced ischemic stroke by 26% in patients after a non-cardioembolic ischemic stroke or high-risk TIA, compared to antiplatelet therapy alone. The reduction was observed alongside a similar rate of ISTH-classified bleeding between asundexian and placebo. The treatment effect for the primary endpoint remained consistent across key subgroups, including age, sex, type of index event, non-cardioembolic stroke subtypes, stroke severity, and planned antiplatelet therapy, supporting the drug’s potential use across a broad patient population.2Full results from Oceanic-stroke have been published in The New England Journal of Medicine.Why does this mechanism matter for stroke prevention?Factor XIa is a protein in the blood coagulation pathway that plays differing roles in hemostasis and thrombosis, and is thought to contribute to pathological thrombus growth and vessel blockage, but plays only a minor role in forming the hemostatic plug that seals a vessel injury.1 Asundexian selectively inhibits Factor XIa, which allows it to reduce pathological clot formation while maintaining a similar rate of ISTH major bleeding compared to placebo, effectively uncoupling hemostasis from pathological thrombosis.Ashkan Shoamanesh, M.D., co-principal investigator of the Oceanic-stroke clinical study and senior scientist at Population Health Research Institute, a Joint Institute of Hamilton Health Sciences and McMaster University, Ontario, Canada, says the risk of a second stroke is highest in the days and weeks after an initial event and persists over time. “I believe asundexian introduces an important new addition to post-stroke care that can be used to help patients reduce the risk of a secondary stroke,” Shoamanesh said.What comes next for asundexian beyond the U.S.?Alongside its FDA approval, Asundexian was also recently approved by China’s National Medical Products Administration (NMPA), with Bayer also submitting the drug for marketing authorization in additional markets around the world, with those applications currently under review.1Bayer says it expects to continue working with health authorities worldwide as it seeks to bring asundexian to patients in other regions, positioning the drug as the first in a new treatment class to reach the global secondary stroke prevention market.1SourcesBayer’s asundexian first FXIa inhibitor approved by U.S. Food and Drug Administration for secondary 关注全球创新药研发管线、临床试验进展与注册审批动态；重点分析热门靶点、临床价值与管线竞争格局。累计发布研发分析 102+ 篇。 19小时前 905 信达生物 信必乐® 托莱西单抗注射液 高胆固醇血症 混合型高脂血症 临床研究 降脂药 11月9日，信达生物宣布，其自主研发的PCSK9单抗 信必乐®（托莱西单抗注射液，IBI306）在单药治疗中国非家族性高胆固醇血症和混合型高脂血症患者的Ⅲ期临床研究（CREDIT-5）中，于第12周达到主要终点及全部关键次要终点。图源：信达生物制药企业官网一、两种给药方案均达主要终点，LDL-C降幅超65%研究显示，托莱西单抗150 mg每2周一次（Q2W）和450 mg每4周一次（Q4W）两种给药方案，治疗第12周LDL-C较基线分别下降65.19%和64.01%，均显著优于安慰剂组（P均＜0.0001）。信达生物计划近期向国家药监局（NMPA）递交该单药治疗适应症的上市申请。图源：摩熵医药-全球药物研发数据库CREDIT-5是一项多中心、随机、双盲、安慰剂对照Ⅲ期研究，共纳入198例中国非家族性高胆固醇血症和混合型高脂血症患者，评估托莱西单抗单药治疗的有效性与安全性。受试者按2:1:2:1的比例随机接受托莱西单抗150 mg Q2W、安慰剂Q2W、托莱西单抗450 mg Q4W或安慰剂Q4W治疗。研究结果显示，治疗第12周，托莱西单抗150 mg Q2W组和450 mg Q4W组LDL-C较基线分别下降65.19%和64.01%，而对应安慰剂组仅下降6.61%和4.31%，差异均具有统计学意义（P均＜0.0001）。此外，托莱西单抗在治疗后2周即表现出LDL-C下降作用。在LDL-C降至2.6 mmol/L以下、1.8 mmol/L以下，以及LDL-C降幅达到50%及以上的受试者比例等关键次要终点上，托莱西单抗组也均显著优于安慰剂组。托莱西单抗Ⅲ期临床试验既往结果数据图图源：摩熵医药-全球药物研发数据库除LDL-C外，托莱西单抗单药治疗还显著改善了非高密度脂蛋白胆固醇（non-HDL-C）、总胆固醇与高密度脂蛋白胆固醇比值（TC/HDL-C）、极低密度脂蛋白胆固醇（VLDL-C）、载脂蛋白B（ApoB）及ApoB/ApoA1比值，脂蛋白(a)［Lp(a)］降幅接近50%。安全性方面，研究期间未发生严重治疗期间出现的不良事件（TEAE），也未出现导致停药或中断研究药物的不良事件，未发现新的安全性信号。二、国产PCSK9单抗拓展单药治疗，拟递交新适应症上市申请托莱西单抗是一款重组全人源抗PCSK9单克隆抗体，可通过特异性结合PCSK9，减少其介导的低密度脂蛋白受体（LDLR）内吞，提高LDLR水平，从而促进LDL-C清除。作为中国首个获批上市并纳入国家医保目录的国产PCSK9抗体药物，信必乐®自2025年1月1日起纳入国家医保目录，至今已惠及超过100万名患者，并获得多部权威临床指南和专家共识推荐。图源：摩熵医药-全球药物研发数据库目前，他汀类药物仍是血脂异常治疗的一线基础用药，但部分患者存在他汀不耐受、降脂效果不佳或难以达到目标值等问题，非他汀类降脂药物因此成为重要的治疗补充。此次CREDIT-5研究成功，进一步为托莱西单抗单药治疗非家族性高胆固醇血症和混合型高脂血症提供了Ⅲ期临床证据。随着新适应症上市申请推进，其临床应用范围有望进一步拓展。 content: 首页 资讯 摩熵原创 注册审批 百济神州daraxonrasib片拟纳入CDE优先审评，全球首款泛RAS(ON)抑制剂冲刺国内胰腺癌适应症 百济神州daraxonrasib片拟纳入CDE优先审评，全球首款泛RAS(ON)抑制剂冲刺国内胰腺癌适应症 张鹏 · 新药研发分析师 张 张鹏 新药研发分析师 审核：王正晴 · 药学博士 关注全球创新药研发管线、临床试验进展与注册审批动态；重点分析热门靶点、临床价值与管线竞争格局。累计发布研发分析 102+ 篇。 20小时前 1211 百济神州 daraxonrasib片 胰腺癌 CDE优先审评 11月9日，CDE官网显示，百济神州申报的daraxonrasib片拟纳入优先审评品种，用于治疗既往至少接受过一种全身治疗，或不适合接受多药全身治疗的转移性胰腺癌成人患者。图源：CDE官网一、百济神州引进，海外已获FDA批准上市Daraxonrasib是由Revolution Medicines开发的一款口服RAS(ON)多选择性非共价三元复合物抑制剂，旨在靶向多种RAS基因型驱动的肿瘤，有望为胰腺癌患者提供新的治疗选择。图源：摩熵医药-全球药物研发数据库该药采用独特的三元复合物作用机制。首先，Daraxonrasib与细胞内伴侣蛋白Cyclophilin A（CypA/PPIA）结合，形成二元复合物；随后进一步结合处于GTP结合活化状态的RAS蛋白，形成RAS-Daraxonrasib-CypA三元复合物。通过这一机制，Daraxonrasib能够抑制野生型和突变型RAS(ON)蛋白与下游效应分子之间的相互作用，进而阻断RAS信号通路。其研发目标是覆盖多种常见RAS基因型驱动的肿瘤，包括胰腺导管腺癌（PDAC）、非小细胞肺癌（NSCLC）和结直肠癌等。2026年8月10日，百济神州与Revolution Medicines达成合作，获得包括Daraxonrasib在内的4款RAS(ON)抑制剂在部分亚洲市场的独家开发及商业化权益。8月26日，Daraxonrasib在美国获FDA批准上市，商品名为RASONQUE，用于治疗既往至少接受过一种全身治疗，或不适合接受多药全身治疗的转移性胰腺导管腺癌成人患者。图源：摩熵医药-全球药物研发数据库二、突破KRAS G12C局限，拓展胰腺癌靶向治疗RAS信号通路是多种实体瘤发生发展的重要驱动因素，也是肿瘤靶向治疗领域长期关注的研发方向。其中，KRAS突变在胰腺导管腺癌中尤为常见，但针对不同RAS突变亚型开发有效药物，仍面临较大挑战。目前，已获批的RAS靶向药物中，部分产品主要针对KRAS G12C突变，包括Sotorasib、Adagrasib、Fulzerasib等，适用的突变亚型相对有限。与之相比，Daraxonrasib采用RAS(ON)多选择性抑制策略，靶向范围不局限于单一KRAS G12C突变，而是针对多种RAS基因型驱动的肿瘤，进一步拓展了RAS靶向治疗的研发方向。此次Daraxonrasib拟纳入CDE优先审评，意味着该药在中国的注册审评取得新进展。随着广谱RAS靶向药物研发持续推进，胰腺癌靶向治疗领域有望迎来更多新的治疗选择。参考来源：[1] CDE官网[2] 摩熵医药（原药融云）数据库扩展阅读：1. 全球首款GPC3/4-1BB双抗挺进III期，百济神州BGB-B2033启动肝细胞癌全球关键性临床2. title: DATA+AI赋能HER2靶点药物全生命周期开发，从病理判读到管线追踪，打通低表达乳腺癌精准诊疗全链条
content: 首页 资讯 摩熵原创 深度分析 DATA+AI赋能HER2靶点药物全生命周期开发，从病理判读到管线追踪，打通低表达乳腺癌精准诊疗全链条 DATA+AI赋能HER2靶点药物全生命周期开发，从病理判读到管线追踪，打通低表达乳腺癌精准诊疗全链条 张鹏 · 新药研发分析师 张 张鹏 新药研发分析师 审核：王正晴 · 药学博士 关注全球创新药研发管线、临床试验进展与注册审批动态；重点分析热门靶点、临床价值与管线竞争格局。累计发布研发分析 102+ 篇。 19小时前 960 HER2 正大天晴 DATA+AI 乳腺癌 精准诊疗 2026年ESMO年会上，正大天晴HER2双表位ADC TQB2102的Ⅲ期研究入选LBA口头报告，HER2低表达乳腺癌人群中位PFS达16.4个月。行业聚焦HER2低表达/超低表达精准识别，DATA+AI可辅助病理判读、临床证据分析，覆盖HER2靶点药物全研发周期。2026年10月23日，在ESMO年会上，正大天晴HER2双表位ADC TQB2102的Ⅲ期研究APEX-Breast01入选LBA优选口头报告。[8]图1 APEX-Breast01会议摘要HR阳性/HER2低表达复发或转移性乳腺癌人群中，试验组与化疗组中位PFS分别为16.4个月和5.5个月，风险比为0.29。[7]图2 APEX-Breast01疗效结果这项进展让HER2低表达领域再次受到关注。随着治疗探索深入，如何识别潜在获益患者，也成为药物开发必须面对的问题。从HER2-low到HER2-ultralow，表达状态的进一步细分，牵动着患者筛选、临床研究与市场判断。AI能否帮助识别微弱信号，是其中一个切口；对于药企，更值得关注的是，如何沿着HER2这一核心靶点，将AI应用延伸到研发、临床与商业化。一、治疗边界拓展，患者如何识别？TQB2102的上述结果体现了HER2-low人群的治疗进展；HER2-ultralow的治疗意义，则可从德曲妥珠单抗的适应症拓展中理解。据摩熵医药全球药物研发数据库显示，2025年1月，美国FDA批准德曲妥珠单抗用于特定HR阳性、HER2-low或HER2-ultralow不可切除或转移性乳腺癌患者，该类患者需在转移性疾病阶段接受一种或多种内分泌治疗后出现疾病进展，且HER2状态须经批准的检测方法确认。[1]图3 摩熵医药-全球药物研发数据库HER2-low通常指IHC 1+或IHC 2+/ISH阴性；而上述适应症中的HER2-ultralow指IHC 0但存在膜染色。它并非新增的独立IHC评分类别，而是对IHC 0人群中存在膜染色者的进一步描述。2023年ASCO/CAP指南沿用既有IHC评分体系，未将HER2-low或HER2-ultralow设为独立评分类别。[2]需要区分的是，TQB2102上述研究聚焦HER2-low，不能据此推断其在HER2-ultralow人群中的疗效。不同药物的机制、适应症及研究人群存在差异，检测结果需要放在具体治疗条件下解读。对药企而言，检测定义已经成为连接药物证据与目标患者的重要条件。二、微弱信号，为何难以判准？一项纳入中国10家医院、2869例乳腺癌患者的多中心研究显示，历史检测结果与重新判读结果的一致率存在明显差异：HER2-ultralow为43.3%，而HER2-low一致率为91.7%。这提示HER2-ultralow状态在两次结果之间的一致性较低，但不能直接解释为误诊率。[3]图4 HER2分类一致率判读分歧集中在是否存在膜染色及其比例。微弱、局灶的染色可能受到背景干扰，组织异质性也会增加判断难度，单张切片不能代表肿瘤所有区域或不同时间的表达状态。另一项单中心研究也观察到低表达区间的阅片者差异，单次教学后整体一致性未见改善。[4]对药企而言，检测差异可能改变入组人群，也会影响试验比较和目标市场测算。因此，分析HER2新药进展时，需要同时核对检测方法、患者定义及复核流程，明确研究结果适用于哪些人群。由此也引出一个问题：AI能否提升判读一致性，并进一步支持药企开展证据分析？三、从看清信号到看懂机会AI如何服务药企？临床开发：从判读辅助到证据分析针对HER2 IHC判读中的低表达及HER2-ultralow识别难点，2025年一项多国观察性研究显示，AI辅助后，病理医生对五类HER2结果的平均观察者间一致率由64.3%升至80.0%，与参考评分相符的平均准确率由69.3%升至73.8%。前者反映医生之间判读是否一致，后者反映判读结果与参考评分是否相符，均不能直接推断患者疗效改善。[5]图5 AI辅助前后判读表现同年另一项AI辅助培训研究中，病理医生与中心参考评分的一致率由76.3%升至89.6%，HER2-ultralow被判为null（该研究中指IHC 0且无膜染色）的比例由29.5%降至4.0%。[6]图6 AI辅助培训研究结果两项研究的设计、培训流程及病例条件不同，不能直接比较提升幅度；第二项研究中，培训、讨论与测试病例变化同时存在，改善也不能全部归因于AI。这些结果提示AI具有辅助识别和量化的潜力，但仍需跨实验室、染色平台及扫描设备验证，不能替代病理医生复核。从病理图像判读走向临床开发，AI处理的对象也随之拓展：除图像外，还包括研究文献与临床资料。药企需要判断已有结果是否适用于自身目标人群，以及不同研究设计会如何影响方案选择。AI可辅助提取HER2试验的评分标准、中心要求、既往治疗、治疗线数及终点，形成证据矩阵，为临床方案讨论提供参考。例如，两项HER2 ADC研究即使都纳入HER2-low人群，也可能在HR状态、既往治疗、样本来源和对照方案上存在差异。AI可帮助标记这些条件，减少跨研究比较时的信息遗漏。仅凭PFS等终点数值，仍不足以判断产品优劣。在获得授权且数据质量满足要求的前提下，AI还可辅助整理临床与病理资料，支持探索性的患者分层和疗效关联分析。涉及医学判断、入组决策及GCP要求的事项，仍需专业人员审核。从辅助病理判读和临床证据分析出发，DATA+AI还可整合研发、临床和市场数据，为药企的研发立项、BD评估与商业化决策提供参考。研发与BD端，企业需要结合HER2 ADC的抗体表位、内吞特征、连接子、载荷及药物抗体比等设计要素，评估候选产品的差异，以及其在低抗原密度下的递送能力、活性与安全性表现。AI可在具备适用模型和数据的前提下，辅助开展序列与结构分析，并关联论文、专利、临床试验登记及企业披露，追踪竞品管线、整理资产证据；相关预测仍需实验验证，资产估值与交易判断也需结合权益范围、开发成本和商业假设。进入商业化阶段，HER2-low或HER2-ultralow人群比例并不直接等同于产品的可及市场，还需结合适应症、治疗线数、检测可及性及支付准入条件逐层测算，并进一步分析区域潜力、医院诊疗与用药基础及竞争变化。AI可辅助建立可调整、可追溯的分析情景，为市场进入和资源配置提供参考。摩熵DATA+AI：让数据进入药企业务流程上述场景的共同基础，是可靠的数据来源、统一口径与可追溯的分析过程。药企可先从临床证据整理、管线追踪或市场分析等明确任务切入，将专业数据接入业务流程。摩熵医药DATA+AI以50亿+结构化医药数据为底座，结合大语言模型、RAG、垂域多模态及知识库、知识图谱能力，支持融合企业内部数据，构建药物全生命周期智能应用。结合企业的数据条件与业务流程，可围绕HER2建设以下应用。分子设计等专业预测任务，则需按具体需求匹配模型与验证体系。一是建立靶点情报智能体，关联药物、企业、适应症与研究，持续追踪研发、临床和注册变化。出现新结果时，辅助提取要点、标记证据版本，为研发和BD团队提供检索与分析依据。二是建设临床证据知识库，关联公开研究与企业授权的方案、报告等资料，围绕表达状态、患者特征和研究结果开展检索。通过保留来源、版本与适用条件，帮助团队核对结论，减少重复查找与口径偏差。三是构建市场分析应用，结合销售与医院资料，从全国、省份下钻至市/区/县、医院，研究区域潜力、终端表现与竞争变化；科室级分析按品种与条件评估。再与企业内部业务数据结合，为市场进入和资源配置提供依据。企业可按需采用数据定制、标准化MCP接口、系统集成与私有化部署，让专业数据进入日常业务流程。这些应用应围绕明确任务验证：信息提取是否准确，引用能否追溯，更新是否及时，分析是否保留关键限定条件。先解决一个具体问题，再逐步扩展，更容易评估实际价值。图7 摩熵DATA+AI应用场景结语回到HER2-ultralow，现有研究提示，AI在部分研究中能够改善判读一致性或准确率，但其稳定性及对临床决策的实际影响仍需进一步验证，AI也不能替代病理医生复核。对于药企，AI的应用不止于病理图像，还可以延伸至证据整理、研发与BD情报分析及商业化测算。其价值最终取决于数据质量、证据可追溯性，以及能否在具体业务流程中为专业人员提供可靠支持。 The biotech PepGen said Tuesday that its experimental drug had shown, by one key measure, the most promising early data yet in the race to treat a muscle disorder that affects over 100,000 people in the U.S. and Europe. title: FDA Requests Updated Safety Label Warning Across All GLP-1 Receptor Agonist for Potential Risk of NAION
content: Advertisement News|Articles|November 10, 2026 FDA Requests Updated Safety Label Warning Across All GLP-1 Receptor Agonist for Potential Risk of NAION Author(s)Nicholas Jacobus FDA is requiring manufacturers of all GLP-1 receptor agonists to add a warning for a potential increased risk of NAION. Advertisement FDA is requiring manufacturers of all glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonist (GLP-1 RA) medications to update the warnings and precautions section of their labeling describing a potential increased risk of non-arteritic anterior ischemic optic neuropathy (NAION).NAION is a rare condition that can cause acute, painless, decreased vision in one eye, including permanent vision loss.1 The requirement touches a drug class with broad reach across both diabetes and obesity care, with GLP-1 RAs mimicking the effects of GLP-1, released by the intestine that lowers blood glucose after eating and acts on parts of the brain that control appetite and food intake.The class is widely used to treat type 2 diabetes and maintain reduced body weight, with several individual medications in the class carrying additional approved uses such as;Reducing the risk of major cardiovascular events including death, heart attack, or stroke in adults with known heart disease and either obesity/overweight or type 2 diabetes.Treating metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis with moderate-to-advanced liver fibrosis.1Lowering the risk of worsening kidney disease, kidney failure, and cardiovascular death in adults with type 2 diabetes and chronic kidney disease.Treating moderate to severe obstructive sleep apnea in adults with obesity. Mark Bagnall, CEO of Phenomix, told Pharmaceutical Executive earlier this year that “those of us who are in the business owe it to patients to let them be fully aware that these risks exist.”FDA is advising patients and caregivers to contact a health care professional immediately if any of these symptoms occur. For patients who have already had a NAION event, FDA is recommending a discuss with their health care professional whether to continue or stop their GLP-1 RA.1What evidence led FDA to this conclusion?FDA’s review was prompted in part by a July 2024 article titled “Risk of Nonarteritic Anterior Ischemic Optic Neuropathy in Patients Prescribed Semaglutide.” examining the risk of NAION in patients prescribed semaglutide.1 While the agency identified limitations in that study, it determined further assessment was warranted and undertook a comprehensive evaluation of clinical trial data, animal data, and postmarketing data, including observational studies and case reports, along with a review of adverse event reports submitted through FDA’s Adverse Event Monitoring System.1A review of available animal data did not identify a mechanism by which GLP-1 RA use could increase NAION risk, so FDA then conducted a meta-analysis of 126 randomized, controlled clinical trials across GLP-1 RA development programs, covering 134,253 patients and 288,879 person-years of exposure. The analysis identified 15 probable NAION events: ten in patients treated with GLP-1 RAs, five in patients on placebo, and none in patients receiving a non-GLP-1 RA glucose-lowering medication.1The resulting incidence rate was 6.4 NAION cases per 100,000 person-years among GLP-1 RA users, compared with 3.8 cases per 100,000 person-years among comparator-treated patients; published literature put the background incidence of NAION in the general population at 2.3 to 10.2 cases per 100,000 persons per year in adults over 50.1FDA separately conducted a retrospective cohort study using its Sentinel Real-World Evidence Data Enterprise Commercial Network, examining adults with type 2 diabetes who started a GLP-1 RA, an SGLT-2 inhibitor, or a DPP-4 inhibitor between 2019 and 2024. Incidence rates in that study ranged from 26 to 32 events per 100,000 person-years. GLP-1 RA use showed no statistically significant increase in NAION risk compared with SGLT-2 inhibitors (hazard ratio 1.19, 95% confidence interval 0.91–1.54), but did show an increased risk compared with DPP-4 inhibitors (hazard ratio 1.43, 95% confidence interval 1.02–2.01).Based on the totality of this evidence, FDA concluded there is a potential increased risk of rare NAION events associated with GLP-1 RA use and is requiring the labeling update across the class.1SourcesFDA Requires Safety Labeling Changes for Glucagon-Like Peptide-1 Receptor Agonists (GLP-1 RAs) Due to Potential Increased Risk of Rare But Serious Eye Condition U.S. Food and Drug Association November 9, 2026, https://www.fda.gov/drugs/drug-safety-communications/fda-requires-safety-labeling-changes-glucagon-peptide-1-receptor-agonists-glp-1-ras-due-potentialFDA orders new warning on GLP-1s over rare eye condition linked to sudden blindness NBC News November 9, 2026, https://www.nbcnews.com/health/health-care/fda-orders-new-warning-glp-1s-rare-eye-condition-linked-sudden-blindne-rcna608309 Newsletter Lead with insight with the Pharmaceutical Executive newsletter, featuring strategic analysis, leadership trends, and market intelligence for biopharma decision-makers. The FDA collects user fees from pharmaceutical companies to fund the agency’s reviews of their medicines.
